title: verify asks for a new approval on every ticket for the same command
desc:
Every ticket asks for a fresh verify approval even when nothing new would run. A plan's verify list typically ends with `python lib/wb.py sdd audit <KEY>`; approvals are verbatim strings (verify.entries), so WB-26, WB-27 and WB-29 each stopped on an approval for the same command with a different key. An approval that is asked for every time for the same thing trains people to approve without reading -- the failure the gate exists to prevent.

Two routes, and why the obvious one is wrong:
- Treating `wb` itself as pre-approved is unsafe: `python lib/wb.py` in a checkout is whatever file that repo ships, not this plugin. Only this repo happens to be the tool.
- Recommended: approve with the ticket's own key abstracted. When a command contains the key of the plan being verified as a whole token, the approval entry records it as `<KEY>` (e.g. `python lib/wb.py sdd audit <KEY>`), and matching substitutes only that plan's key. A different key, or the key inside a longer token, is a different command and asks again.

ACCEPTANCE:
- verify.entries renders the plan's own key as <KEY> in each entry; unapproved() and approve() match on that form
- an approval given for WB-1 covers WB-2 running the same command with its own key, and nothing else (another key, a changed flag, a changed env value all ask again)
- the key is replaced only as a whole token (ABC-1 inside ABC-12 or foo-ABC-1 is left alone)
- the --approve call printed by impl verify names the <KEY> form, so the person approves what will be stored
- existing verbatim approvals keep working
- regression tests for each rule; docs/execution.md approval section updated
